_nota: Prueba inicial y final: mismos 5 conceptos con preguntas distintas (pruebas paralelas). Caso Artemis-7: escenario nuevo calificado con rúbrica 0–8 (4 criterios × 0–2).

inicial.intro: Before lift-off, we want to know what you already know. There are 5 questions and they don't count toward your grade: answer what you think.

preguntas.texto: On a lunar base, oxygen is made by splitting water with electricity. If the electricity runs out, what happens first?
To make oxygen on the base, what is used up besides energy?
The Space Station recycles almost all the water it uses. Without a recycler, a long mission would need…
About how long is the night on the Moon (away from the poles)?
opciones: There is no night on the Moon

preguntas.texto: Satellites warn that a solar storm will reach the Moon tomorrow. What is safest for the crew?
opciones: Go exploring today before it arrives
Nothing: the Moon has an atmosphere that protects

final.intro: You completed the missions! Answer these 5 questions to see how much you learned. At the end you will see the answers with their NASA data.

preguntas.texto: A base's electrolyzer has no power for 3 days. Which resource starts going down without being replaced?
preguntas.explicacion: The electrolyzer makes the oxygen the crew breathes. Without power it makes none, and each astronaut still breathes 0.82 kg per day.

preguntas.texto: A team needs to make 10 kg of oxygen by electrolysis. About how much water will it use?
preguntas.explicacion: To make 1 kg of oxygen, 1.125 kg of water is split (2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂). So 10 kg of O₂ costs about 11 kg of water.

preguntas.texto: The water recycler breaks down for 3 days. What happens to the water on those days?
opciones: All the water used is lost
preguntas.explicacion: With the recycler, 98 % of used water is recovered; without it, 100 % is lost. That is why it is wise to carry a reserve for breakdowns.

preguntas.texto: A base in the Sea of Tranquility has only solar panels and a few batteries. When is it in the most danger?
opciones: During the lunar night, about 15 days long
preguntas.explicacion: At night the panels produce nothing, and the lunar night lasts almost 15 Earth days. You need to store a lot of energy or have a reactor that works day and night.

preguntas.texto: Regolith shielding protects every day, but it is very heavy. The shelter protects more during a solar storm, but…
opciones: That day the crew does no science
It uses up all the water
preguntas.explicacion: Every decision has a cost: inside the shelter the crew is protected, but they don't go out to explore. That is why it is used only when the storm arrives.

caso.intro: You didn't design this base. Read its logbook and answer as a commander. Each answer is scored from 0 to 2 points.
caso.descripcion: A base at the Moon's equator with 4 astronauts. They brought 8 solar panels, 1 battery, a water recycler and 100 kg of water. No reactor.
bitacora: Days 1–5: everything normal, the Sun is shining and there is spare energy.
Day 7: the battery runs empty. The electrolyzer shuts down.
Day 10: the oxygen reserve runs out. The mission fails.

criterios.texto: What was the main cause of the failure?

opciones.porque: That is what happened at the end (the effect), but it doesn't explain why.

opciones.texto: They had no energy for the long lunar night
opciones.porque: Exactly: without energy at night the electrolyzer shut down and no new oxygen was made.
Food doesn't appear in the logbook.
There was no solar storm on this mission.

criterios.texto: Which change fixes the problem best?

opciones.porque: At night panels produce nothing, no matter how many you have.
It helps for a few days, but it's a patch: the base still has no power at night.

opciones.texto: Add a reactor or batteries for about 15 days of night
opciones.porque: It tackles the cause: the base has energy through the whole lunar night.
It saves energy, but you would lose almost all your water.

criterios.texto: Which NASA fact best supports your change?

opciones.texto: The Moon's gravity is one sixth of Earth's
opciones.porque: It's a real fact, but it has nothing to do with this failure.

opciones.texto: The ISS recycles 98 % of its water
opciones.porque: True, but water wasn't the problem.

opciones.texto: An astronaut breathes 0.82 kg of oxygen per day
opciones.porque: It explains how much oxygen is missing, but not why the reactor or batteries are the answer.

opciones.texto: The lunar night lasts ~15 days and NASA's reactor gives 40 kW day and night
opciones.porque: It directly justifies the change: you must cover 15 days without Sun.

criterios.texto: If you add the reactor (6 tonnes), what else do you have to consider?

opciones.texto: Nothing: the reactor only has advantages
opciones.porque: Everything has a cost on a space base.

opciones.texto: The mass: I may need to remove something else to stay under the rocket's limit
opciones.porque: Exactly: everything is connected. You gain energy, but lose room for other things.
The opposite: it works day and night.

opciones.texto: That its temperature and maintenance must be watched
opciones.porque: Reasonable, but the main effect on your design is the mass.
